\title{Proof-Gap Protocol for Source-Faithful Formalization}
\author{}
\date{2026-05-11}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Purpose}

This note fixes terminology for a recurring failure mode in the formalization
of the low individual degree test paper, \path{arXiv:2009.12982}.  It
complements the note-writing policy in \path{docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex} and
the source-statement audit tracked historically in \ghissue{1458}.  The current
source-boundary proof holes are tracked in \ghissue{1507} and \ghissue{422}.
A proof may be blocked at
an intermediate mathematical assertion.  If that assertion is added as a new
hypothesis to a theorem labelled as a paper theorem, the resulting \Lean{}
theorem
may be correct as a conditional statement, but it is no longer the theorem in
the cited source.  The apparent proof has not closed the paper theorem; it has
moved a proof obligation into the theorem statement.

The protocol below distinguishes such proof debt from legitimate formal
boundary conditions and from genuine mathematical corrections.  It is meant for
contributors and reviewers who must decide whether a bridge, residual, repair,
input, or obligation structure is a proved local construction, a tracked proof
gap, or statement drift which must be repaired before a theorem may be
advertised as a source theorem.  The default rule is restrictive: such data
must not be added to a paper-facing theorem unless it is part of the cited
source statement or a documented faithful encoding of its ambient hypotheses.

\section{Basic objects}

\paragraph{Source theorem.}
A source theorem is a theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary in the paper
source under \path{references/ldt-paper/}.  Its hypotheses and conclusion are
the mathematical ground truth, subject only to faithful formal encoding and to
documented paper-gap corrections.

\paragraph{Paper-facing declaration.}
A \Lean{} declaration is paper-facing when it is named or cited as the
formalization of a source theorem, for instance through a blueprint
\verb|\lean{}| link on a theorem environment carrying a paper label.  Such a
declaration must match the source theorem in its public statement.  In
particular, it may not add an unproved bridge, residual, repair, input,
obligation structure, or other proof-obligation hypothesis which the paper does
not assume.

\paragraph{Proof obligation.}
A proof obligation is an intermediate assertion needed by the proof of a source
theorem.  It may be a construction, an estimate, a transport lemma, or a
comparison between two formal representations.  If the paper proves or invokes
this assertion, then the formalization should state it as a separate lemma or
theorem and prove it from the upstream hypotheses.

\paragraph{Obligation discharger.}
An obligation discharger is a theorem or definition which constructs a proof
obligation from the paper hypotheses already available at that point in the
argument.  This is the preferred representation of missing work.  If the proof
is not yet complete, the discharger may temporarily contain a tracked
\verb|sorry|, but the paper-facing theorem should call it rather than assume
its output as an additional theorem hypothesis.

\paragraph{Conditional helper.}
A conditional helper is a separately named theorem whose statement explicitly
assumes a proof obligation.  Names such as
\leanid{mainFormal\_ofInternalObligations},
\leanid{orthonormalization\_ofInput}, or names whose suffix advertises the
assumed obligation are permitted only when the declaration is not presented as
the source theorem.  A conditional helper is a quarantine for downstream proof
content; it does not close the source theorem.

\section{Bridge, residual, repair, input, and obligation structures}

The words \emph{bridge}, \emph{residual}, \emph{repair}, \emph{input}, and
\emph{obligation structure} name possible formal shapes.  They become dangerous
when their mathematical status is unclear or when their names make unproved
data look like acceptable hypotheses of a source theorem.

\paragraph{Bridge.}
A bridge should be a transport theorem between two already defined
mathematical forms: for example, a tensor-placement identity, a conversion
between two equivalent consistency relations, or a statement translating a
source object into a formal representation.  A bridge is harmless only after it
is proved from previously available assumptions.  It becomes proof debt when it
is assumed because the transport has not yet been proved.  It becomes theorem
drift when the assumed bridge is added to a paper-facing theorem.

\paragraph{Residual.}
A residual is a named remainder after part of an argument has been performed.
It is often a useful way to record the exact missing target after a completed
construction.  A residual may appear as the conclusion of a helper theorem or
as the input of a quarantined conditional helper.  It is not a permissible new
assumption on a paper theorem unless the paper itself assumes that residual.

\paragraph{Input.}
An input is a named bundle of data or hypotheses consumed by a construction or
conditional helper.  It is harmless only when each load-bearing field is either
part of the source hypotheses or is produced by an earlier theorem.  It becomes
proof debt when the bundle is merely assumed because the construction of its
fields is missing.  It becomes theorem drift when such a bundle is added to the
public statement of a source theorem.

\paragraph{Repair.}
A repair is a mathematical construction which replaces an approximate or
partial object by a better object, usually with a quantitative estimate.  In
the low individual degree test formalization, projectivization and
orthonormalization repairs are genuine mathematical operations.  A repair
should therefore appear as a construction or as a theorem discharging the
corresponding obligation.  If a theorem assumes the output of the repair instead
of constructing it, that theorem is conditional on the repair.

\paragraph{Obligation structure.}
An obligation structure is a record whose fields are the data and estimates
needed by a later construction.  This is acceptable only as an internal target
or as a hypothesis of a conditional helper.  Such a structure becomes statement
drift if it is added to a paper-facing theorem instead of being constructed
inside the proof.  The review question is whether every load-bearing field is
proved from the source hypotheses or is explicitly tracked as a missing
obligation.

\section{The main failure mode}

Suppose the paper proves
\[
  H \Longrightarrow C.
\]
During formalization, the proof may need an intermediate assertion \(B\).  The
paper theorem should be represented as
\[
  H \Longrightarrow B \Longrightarrow C
  \quad\text{inside the proof,}
\]
where \(B\) is obtained by a lemma or theorem from \(H\).  The following
public statement is a different theorem:
\[
  H \land B \Longrightarrow C.
\]
It is not unsound in \Lean{}, but it is not the paper theorem.  It says that the
conclusion follows if the missing bridge data is supplied.  Such a theorem is a
conditional helper, even if its conclusion looks exactly like the paper's
conclusion.

This is the situation colloquially described as ``adding a bridge
hypothesis''.  More precisely, an unproved intermediate step has been promoted
from the proof body to the theorem's assumptions.  The correction is not to hide
the hypothesis under a different structure name.  The correction is to keep a
paper-facing theorem with the source statement and move the missing step to a
named internal proof obligation.

\section{Faithful boundary hypotheses}

Not every extra formal hypothesis is a theorem drift.  Some hypotheses are
faithful boundary conditions introduced by formal encoding.  Examples include
nonnegativity needed for a real power, positivity needed to divide by a
quantity, finiteness and nonemptiness of an index type, a field-model instance,
or decidability instances required by \Lean{}.  Such hypotheses are acceptable
when they express part of the mathematical ambient setting or make explicit a
condition used implicitly in the paper.

The distinction is load-bearing.  A faithful boundary hypothesis describes the
domain in which the paper's objects live.  A proof-debt hypothesis supplies a
mathematical step that the proof should derive.  If removing the hypothesis
leaves an unproved construction or estimate from the paper proof, then the
hypothesis is proof debt, not a boundary condition.

\section{Definition drift and subtree repair}

Definition drift is especially dangerous because it propagates.  If a
definition is changed so that it no longer denotes the object in the paper,
then every downstream theorem using that definition may continue to compile
while proving statements about the wrong object.  Downstream theorem statements
can then be repaired piecemeal, but the development remains unstable because
the wrong definition is still upstream.

When a definition mismatch is found, the repair should proceed by a subtree
protocol.

\begin{enumerate}
  \item Identify the source object and the formal object precisely.
  \item Freeze a source-faithful definition or state an adapter theorem
  relating the existing definition to the source object.
  \item Recheck the downstream theorem chain against that definition or adapter.
  \item Re-formalize the affected subtree from the corrected interface, rather
  than adding local hypotheses to each downstream theorem.
  \item If a downstream proof cannot be completed, record the missing obligation
  at the lowest point where the paper proof needs it.
\end{enumerate}

This is slower than editing a final theorem signature, but it prevents a local
definition error from becoming a global theorem-statement error.

\section{Allowed shapes}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{p{0.24\linewidth}p{0.31\linewidth}p{0.32\linewidth}}
\textbf{Shape} & \textbf{Allowed use} & \textbf{Forbidden use} \\
\hline
Paper-facing theorem & Matches the source statement up to faithful encoding &
Carries non-paper bridge, residual, repair, input, obligation-structure, or
proof-obligation hypotheses \\
Source-shaped theorem with a tracked \verb|sorry| & Default repair when the
source proof is blocked but the statement is known & Replaced by a strengthened
theorem statement merely to keep the file compiling \\
Conditional helper & Temporary quarantine for substantial proof content whose
remaining named obligation has not yet been discharged & Introduced merely to
avoid a \verb|sorry|, or linked as the source theorem or marked as
proof-complete for that theorem \\
Obligation discharger theorem & Constructs the obligation from paper hypotheses &
Merely restates the obligation as an assumption \\
Input bundle & Collects produced data for a local construction & Is assumed by a
source theorem instead of being produced \\
Obligation structure & Bundles constructed data and estimates & Hides unproved
fields that are then assumed by a source theorem \\
Paper-gap note & Documents a real mathematical or formal-statement divergence &
Justifies silent statement drift without a repair plan
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\section{Protocol for a blocked proof}

When a source-labelled proof is blocked, use the following order.

\begin{enumerate}
  \item Read the cited source statement and the proof passage in
  \path{references/ldt-paper/}.
  \item Write the paper theorem form, the current \Lean{} theorem form, and the
  first missing intermediate assertion.
  \item Decide whether the missing assertion is a faithful boundary condition,
  a representation adapter, an ordinary lemma from the paper proof, or a real
  paper-gap discrepancy.
  \item If it is an ordinary lemma or adapter, create a named theorem which
  discharges that obligation.  Do not add it to the source theorem as a new
  hypothesis.
  \item Keep the source-labelled theorem itself in the source form, even if its
  proof must contain a tracked \verb|sorry|.  This is the default repair when
  the missing assertion has not yet been proved.
  \item Create a conditional helper only to quarantine substantial proof content
  that already exists and would otherwise be lost.  Do not create such a helper
  merely to avoid a \verb|sorry| or to keep making progress.  If a conditional
  helper remains, give it a conditional name, keep it separate from the
  paper-facing theorem, and record the obligation discharger that must eliminate
  it.
  \item If the source and formal statements genuinely differ, write or update a
  note under \path{docs/paper-gaps/} before marking the statement as aligned.
  \item Update the blueprint so that paper labels point only to paper-facing
  declarations.  Conditional helpers belong in remarks or implementation
  notes, not in the source theorem block.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Retirement criterion}

An auxiliary declaration should be removed from the main blueprint route, or
renamed and documented as a purely internal lemma, when all three of the
following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item it is not a statement in the cited paper and is not an explicitly cited
        outside result;
  \item no current proof of a paper-level target needs it as stated;
  \item it assumes stronger proof data, finite-length data, completion data,
        repair data, synchronization data, or package fields than the paper
        proof requires.
\end{enumerate}
If such a declaration is still useful as a formal intermediate result, it
should remain a lemma or a visibly conditional helper with a planned discharge.
It should not be a headline replacement for the paper theorem, and it should
not support a source-labelled blueprint \verb|\leanok| claim.

\section{Review questions}

A reviewer should first compare every paper-labelled declaration with the cited
source statement, checking both hypotheses and conclusion up to faithful formal
encoding.  Bridge, residual, repair, input, obligation-structure, and
proof-obligation assumptions should be absent from paper-facing theorem
signatures unless they occur in the paper.  If a conditional helper remains,
its name should be explicitly conditional and it should not support a source
theorem \verb|\leanok| claim.
Each load-bearing obligation-structure or input field should have a theorem
discharging it, a tracked issue, or an explicit \verb|sorry| at the obligation
site.  When a definition has changed, the downstream subtree should be checked
against the corrected definition rather than patched locally.  Finally, if the
formal statement genuinely differs from the source statement, a paper-gap note
should explain the mathematical difference and give a plan to remove or justify
it.

\section{Conclusion}

The project should prefer visible proof obligations over invisible statement
drift.  A tracked \verb|sorry| in the source-shaped theorem, or in the lowest
named internal obligation needed by its proof, is less misleading than a source
theorem whose assumptions have been strengthened.  Conditional helpers are not a
normal substitute for unfinished proofs; they are temporary quarantines for
substantial proof content, and they must remain conditional until the missing
obligation is discharged.  The paper-facing declaration is reserved for the
theorem proved by the paper, or for a documented corrected version whose
mathematical difference is explicit.

\end{document}

  Then the conclusion of the source theorem form holds with $\sqrt\eps$
  replaced by $\eta = \sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta$ throughout: the state is
  $O(\eta)$-close to $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2} \ot \ket{\aux}$, the four
  measurement relations and the two anticommutation consequences hold with
  $\approx_\eta$.  A symmetric strategy whose $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$
  measurements are consistent on $\ket{\psi}$ has $\Delta_1 = \Delta_5 = 0$,
  so the class of symmetric consistent strategies fixed by the owner decision
  is the case $\delta = 0$, in which the error scale is the source's
  $\sqrt\eps$. The bit effects in this form use the relabeling described
  above; Section~\ref{sec:prescribed} compares them with the prescribed answers.
  Symmetry is not assumed: the proof does not use it, and the
  source's application does not have it in the form the formalization needs
  (Section~\ref{sec:sufficiency}).
\end{enumerate}
The formal declaration carrying the corrected form is
\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists\_ms\_rigidity}, with the witness and distance
definitions \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.MsRigidityWitness},
\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msOperatorDistanceA},
\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msOperatorDistanceB}, and
\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msAnticommutatorDistanceA} in
\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems.lean}, and the defect

\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems/Rigidity/Consistency.lean}.
The specialization to symmetric consistent strategies --- which are
projective, consistency of a strategy being defined only for projective
strategies in \path{def:consistent-strategy} --- is
\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists\_ms\_rigidity\_of\_symmetric\_consistent}.

\section{The source assertion}

The Magic Square game $\game^{\MS}$ of \cite[Section~7]{Ji2020MIPStar} has nine
variables $x_1,\ldots,x_9$ over $\F_2$ in a $3\times 3$ grid and six parity
constraints, one per row and column.  Its verifier samples a uniformly random
edge $\Constraint_i \,\text{---}\, \Variable_j$ of the bipartite incidence
graph and sends one endpoint to a uniformly random player and the other
endpoint to the other player.  The constraint player answers with an
assignment to the three variables of its constraint, the variable player with
one bit, and the players win when the assignment satisfies the constraint and
the two reported values of $x_j$ agree.  Two features are used below: the game
is \emph{role-symmetric}, so each player is asked constraint questions and
variable questions, and its question distribution is supported on
constraint--variable pairs, so the same question is never sent to both
players.

A strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ consists of a unit vector
$\ket{\psi} \in \mH_{\mathrm A} \ot \mH_{\mathrm B}$ and POVMs $\{A^x_a\}$,
$\{B^y_b\}$; $\val^*(\game^{\MS},\strategy)$ is the acceptance probability.
The strategy is \emph{symmetric} when $\mH_{\mathrm A} = \mH_{\mathrm B}$,
$\ket{\psi}$ is invariant under exchanging the two factors, and $A = B$; the
source writes such a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ and states that it
almost always restricts attention to this class.%
\footnote{Definitions and the convention:
\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex}, lines~74--92
and~174.  In this repository: \path{def:symmetric-game} in
\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex}, formalized as
\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.SymmetricStrategy}.}
For operators $M, N$ and a state $\ket{\varphi}$ we write
$M \approx_\zeta N$ for
$\bra{\varphi}(M-N)^\dagger(M-N)\ket{\varphi} \le O(\zeta)$, and for POVM
families $\{M_a\}, \{N_a\}$ for
$\sum_a \bra{\varphi}(M_a-N_a)^\dagger(M_a-N_a)\ket{\varphi} \le O(\zeta)$;
the state is named wherever the relation is used.

The rigidity theorem asserts:%
\footnote{Statement and proof at
\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
lines~620--652; the blueprint statement is \path{thm:ms-rigidity} in
\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex}, now in the corrected form.
Tracked in \ghissue{172}; the refutation is recorded on \ghissue{105}, and the
decisions to record and to repair the statement are items~B4 and~B5 on
\ghissue{26}.}
if $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ succeeds in $\game^{\MS}$ with probability
$1-\eps$, then there are local isometries
$\phi_{\mathrm A} \colon \mH_{\mathrm A} \to \mH_{\mathrm A'} \ot
\mH_{\mathrm A''}$ and
$\phi_{\mathrm B} \colon \mH_{\mathrm B} \to \mH_{\mathrm B'} \ot
\mH_{\mathrm B''}$ with
$\mH_{\mathrm A'}, \mH_{\mathrm B'} \cong (\C^2)^{\ot 2}$, and a state
$\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{\mathrm A''} \ot \mH_{\mathrm B''}$, such that
\begin{equation}
  \bigl\| \phi_{\mathrm A} \ot \phi_{\mathrm B}\ket{\psi}
    - \ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2} \ot \ket{\aux} \bigr\| \le O(\sqrt\eps)
  \tag{\path{thm:ms-rigidity}, 1}
\end{equation}
and, writing $\tilde A^x_a = \phi_{\mathrm A} A^x_a \phi_{\mathrm A}^\dagger$
and $\tilde B^y_b = \phi_{\mathrm B} B^y_b \phi_{\mathrm B}^\dagger$,
\begin{equation}
  \tilde A^{\Variable_1}_b \ot \Id \approx_{\sqrt\eps}
    (\sigma^X_b)_{\mathrm A'} \ot \Id,
  \qquad
  \Id \ot \tilde B^{\Variable_1}_b \approx_{\sqrt\eps}
    \Id \ot (\sigma^X_b)_{\mathrm B'},
  \tag{\path{thm:ms-rigidity}, 2}
\end{equation}
with respect to $\ket{\Theta} = \ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2}_{\mathrm{A'B'}} \ot
\ket{\aux}_{\mathrm{A''B''}}$, together with the two companion relations for
$\Variable_5$ and $\sigma^Z$ and the anticommutation consequence for the
associated observables.

\section{What the conclusion forces}
\label{sec:forces}

Write $O_A = \tilde A^{\Variable_1}_0 - \tilde A^{\Variable_1}_1$ and
$O_B = \tilde B^{\Variable_1}_0 - \tilde B^{\Variable_1}_1$ for the transported
$\pm 1$ observables, and $\mathcal O_A, \mathcal O_B$ for the untransported
ones.  Take $\eps = 0$, so that all the estimates above are exact.  Then
$\phi_{\mathrm A} \ot \phi_{\mathrm B}\ket{\psi} = \ket{\Theta}$, and since
$\phi^\dagger \phi = \Id$ for an isometry, $\tilde M \phi = \phi M$ for each
transported operator, whence
\begin{equation}
  \bra{\psi}\,\mathcal O_A \ot \mathcal O_B\,\ket{\psi}
  = \bra{\Theta}\, O_A \ot O_B \,\ket{\Theta}
  = \bra{\Theta}\, \sigma^X_{\mathrm A'} \ot \sigma^X_{\mathrm B'}
    \,\ket{\Theta}
  = 1 .
  \label{eq:forced-correlation}
\end{equation}
The middle equality uses the exact form of the two relations in
(\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~2) and the self-adjointness of the observables; the
last one is the identity
$\bra{\EPR_2}\, M \ot N \,\ket{\EPR_2} = \tr(M N^{\mathsf T})/2$ applied to
$M = N = \sigma^X$ on the first extracted qubit pair.  For $\pm 1$ observables,
$\bra{\psi} \mathcal O_A \ot \mathcal O_B \ket{\psi} = 1$ is equivalent to
$(\mathcal O_A \ot \Id)\ket{\psi} = (\Id \ot \mathcal O_B)\ket{\psi}$, that is,
to the two players' $\Variable_1$ measurements agreeing on $\ket{\psi}$.  The
conclusion of the theorem therefore contains a cross-player agreement
assertion about a question pair that the game never samples.

\section{A perfect strategy violating the conclusion}
\label{sec:counterexample}

Fix the canonical Mermin--Peres operator solution on
$\mathcal K = \C^2 \ot \C^2$: the nine $\pm 1$ observables
\[
  \begin{array}{ccc}
    \sigma^X \ot \Id & \Id \ot \sigma^X & \sigma^X \ot \sigma^X \\
    \Id \ot \sigma^Z & \sigma^Z \ot \Id & \sigma^Z \ot \sigma^Z \\
    \sigma^X \ot \sigma^Z & \sigma^Z \ot \sigma^X & \sigma^Y \ot \sigma^Y
  \end{array}
\]
placed in the grid, whose rows and first two columns multiply to $\Id$ and
whose third column multiplies to $-\Id$.  All nine are real and symmetric.  Let
$\ket{\Omega} \in \mathcal K \ot \mathcal K$ be the maximally entangled state,
which is $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2}$ after reordering the qubits, and let $M$ be the
measurement family that answers $\Constraint_i$ by jointly measuring the three
commuting observables of row or column $i$ and answers $\Variable_j$ by the
two-outcome measurement $\{(\Id \pm O_j)/2\}$.  Then $(\ket{\Omega}, M)$ is a
symmetric, projective, consistent strategy of value $1$.

Now give each player a copy of $\mathcal K \ot \mathcal K$ and split the two
roles across the two copies: on a constraint question the first player measures
copy~$1$ and the second measures copy~$2$, and on a variable question the first
player measures copy~$2$ and the second measures copy~$1$.  With the state
$\ket{\Omega}_{\mathrm A_1 \mathrm B_1} \ot
\ket{\Omega}_{\mathrm A_2 \mathrm B_2}$, every sampled question pair consists of
one constraint and one variable, so the two measurements actually performed are
the canonical perfect pair acting on a single maximally entangled copy: on
copy~$1$ when the first player holds the constraint, and on copy~$2$ when the
second player does.  The value is therefore $1$.  The two players' $\Variable_1$
observables, however, act on $\mathrm A_2$ and $\mathrm B_1$, whose joint
reduced state is a product of maximally mixed states, so
\begin{equation}
  \bra{\psi}\,\mathcal O_A \ot \mathcal O_B\,\ket{\psi}
  = \frac{\tr(\sigma^X \ot \Id)}{4} \cdot \frac{\tr(\sigma^X \ot \Id)}{4}
  = 0 ,
  \label{eq:zero-correlation}
\end{equation}
contradicting \eqref{eq:forced-correlation}.  The same computation with
$\sigma^Z$ refutes the $\Variable_5$ relations.  The source statement is thus
false at $\eps = 0$, and no choice of isometries or auxiliary state can repair
it, since \eqref{eq:forced-correlation} used only that $\phi_{\mathrm A}$ and
$\phi_{\mathrm B}$ are isometries.  In the terms of \eqref{eq:defect}, this
strategy has $\Delta_1 = \Delta_5 = 1$: for $\pm1$ observables
$\sum_b \|(A_b \ot \Id - \Id \ot B_b)\ket\psi\|^2
= 1 - \bra\psi \mathcal O_A \ot \mathcal O_B \ket\psi$
whenever the two measurements are projective on the state.

\section{Symmetry does not repair the statement}
\label{sec:symmetric}

The strategy just described is not symmetric: the two players use different
measurement families.  It is natural to hope that the source's standing
restriction to symmetric strategies excludes it.  It does not.

Give each player a flag qubit and two copies of $\mathcal K$, so that the local
space is $\C^2 \ot \mathcal K \ot \mathcal K$, and take the state
\[
  \ket{\psi} = \frac{1}{\sqrt2}
    \bigl( \ket{0}_{f_{\mathrm A}}\ket{1}_{f_{\mathrm B}}
         + \ket{1}_{f_{\mathrm A}}\ket{0}_{f_{\mathrm B}} \bigr)
    \ot \ket{\Omega}_{\mathrm A_1 \mathrm B_1}
    \ot \ket{\Omega}_{\mathrm A_2 \mathrm B_2} .
\]
Both players use the single family
\begin{align*}
  M^{\Constraint_i}_a
    &= \ket{0}\!\bra{0}_f \ot (M^{\Constraint_i}_a)_1 \ot \Id_2
     + \ket{1}\!\bra{1}_f \ot \Id_1 \ot (M^{\Constraint_i}_a)_2 , \\
  M^{\Variable_j}_b
    &= \ket{0}\!\bra{0}_f \ot \Id_1 \ot (M^{\Variable_j}_b)_2
     + \ket{1}\!\bra{1}_f \ot (M^{\Variable_j}_b)_1 \ot \Id_2 :
\end{align*}
a player whose flag reads $0$ answers constraints from copy~$1$ and variables
from copy~$2$, and a player whose flag reads $1$ does the opposite.  Since
$\ket{\Omega}$ is invariant under exchanging its two factors, $\ket{\psi}$ is
invariant under exchanging the two players' registers, and the two players use
identical measurements; the strategy is symmetric in the sense of the source.

The flags are perfectly anticorrelated, so on each branch exactly one player
plays the role assigned to flag~$0$.  On the branch $f_{\mathrm A} = 0$, if the
first player receives the constraint it measures copy~$1$ while the second
player, whose flag reads $1$, answers its variable question from copy~$1$ as
well; if the roles are exchanged, both act on copy~$2$.  In every case the pair
of measurements performed is the canonical perfect pair on one maximally
entangled copy, and the branch $f_{\mathrm A} = 1$ is its mirror image.  The
value is again $1$.  The correlation of the two players' $\Variable_1$
observables is, branch by branch, the product of two traces of $\sigma^X \ot
\Id$ against maximally mixed states, hence $0$ as in
\eqref{eq:zero-correlation}, and the cross terms between the two flag branches
vanish because the observables are flag-diagonal.  So
\eqref{eq:forced-correlation} fails for a symmetric strategy of value $1$,
and the same computation refutes the $\Variable_5$ relations.  Again
$\Delta_1 = \Delta_5 = 1$.%
\footnote{This strategy is the player-role symmetrization of the previous one,
so the symmetrization construction of \path{lem:symmetric-strat}
(\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex}, lines~94--130)
does not repair the statement either: it is value-preserving and moves the two
role-dependent families into two blocks of one family, which is exactly what
the flag register does above.}

\section{What the cited self-test provides}

The source imports the theorem from \cite[Theorem~6.9]{Coladangelo2017Robust},
whose notion of robust self-testing is stated for a linear constraint system
game in the ordinary one-way presentation: one player receives a vertex $v$,
that is a constraint, and answers with observables $A^{(v)}_e$ for the
variables $e$ occurring in it, while the other receives a variable $e$ and
answers with an observable $B_e$.%
\footnote{\path{references/cs-paper/self-testing.tex}, lines~669--689 for the
definition and lines~706--724 for the theorem; the Magic Square instance is at
\path{references/cs-paper/specific-games.tex}, lines~111--135.}
The conclusion compares $\phi_{\mathrm A} A^{(v)}_e \phi_{\mathrm A}^\dagger$
with an ideal representation $\tau(e)$ and
$\phi_{\mathrm B} B_e \phi_{\mathrm B}^\dagger$ with its conjugate.  In that
game the first player never receives a bare variable question, so the theorem
constrains one player's constraint observables and the other player's variable
observables, and nothing else.

The source relabels this conclusion for the role-symmetric game, in which each
player has both kinds of question, and asserts it for both players' variable
observables.  The step from the cited conclusion to the printed one is exactly
the cross-player agreement isolated in Section~\ref{sec:forces}, and the
strategies of Sections~\ref{sec:counterexample} and~\ref{sec:symmetric} show
that neither the value hypothesis nor symmetry supplies it.

\section{The correction}
\label{sec:repair}

Recall that a projective measurement $\{M_a\}$ is \emph{consistent} on a state
$\ket{\psi} \in \mH \ot \mH$ when
$(M_a \ot \Id)\ket{\psi} = (\Id \ot M_a)\ket{\psi}$ for every outcome $a$, and
that a \emph{consistent strategy} is a projective strategy all of whose
measurements are consistent; projectivity is part of the source definition and
is used in the computation just below.%
\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex},
lines~144--174; \path{def:consistent-measurement} and
\path{def:consistent-strategy} in
\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex}, formalized as
\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn} and
\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsConsistentStrategyOn}.}
For a symmetric strategy and a two-outcome projective measurement with
observable $\mathcal O = M_0 - M_1$, consistency gives
\[
  \bra{\psi}\, \mathcal O \ot \mathcal O \,\ket{\psi}
  = \bra{\psi}\, (\mathcal O \ot \Id)(\mathcal O \ot \Id) \,\ket{\psi}
  = \bra{\psi}\, \mathcal O^2 \ot \Id \,\ket{\psi} = 1 ,
\]
the last equality using $\mathcal O^2 = \Id$, which holds because $M_0$ and
$M_1$ are complementary projections; for a general two-outcome POVM the
identity fails, as $M_0 = M_1 = \Id/2$ shows, so projectivity is needed at
this step.  The display is precisely the assertion
\eqref{eq:forced-correlation} that the
conclusion forces.  Consistency is thus the missing hypothesis, and it is not an
artefact of the $\eps = 0$ analysis: it is the property that ties the untested
same-question pair to the tested constraint--variable pairs.

\paragraph{The historical correction.}
Owner decision B5 adopted the class of symmetric consistent strategies and
allows a further adjustment provided the corrected statement is both correct
and sufficient for the source's application.  Two observations shape the
adjustment.  First, the proof below uses consistency only for the two
distinguished variable measurements and only in the cross-player form
$(A^{\Variable_j}_b \ot \Id)\ket\psi \approx (\Id \ot B^{\Variable_j}_b)\ket\psi$;
it never uses that $\ket\psi$ is swap-invariant or that $A = B$.  Second, the
source's application (Section~\ref{sec:sufficiency}) does not have exact
consistency: it derives the agreement of the two variable measurements from
the consistency subtests of the Pauli basis test, up to an error of order
$\eps$, and its Lean counterpart is not a symmetric strategy at all.  The
statement is therefore taken in the robust form of item~4 of Section~2: an
arbitrary strategy whose agreement distances \eqref{eq:defect} at
$\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$ are at most $\delta$, with $\sqrt\eps$
replaced by
$\eta = \sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta$ in every estimate of the conclusion.  The
decided class is contained in it as the case $\delta = 0$: for a symmetric
strategy, $\Delta_j = 0$ is exactly the consistency of $\{M^{\Variable_j}_b\}$
on $\ket\psi$ (\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msVariableConsistencyDefect\_eq\_zero\_of\_isConsistent}),
and the error scale is then the source's $\sqrt\eps$. The two
counterexamples have $\Delta_1 = \Delta_5 = 1$, so the hypothesis excludes
them, and at $\eps = \delta = 0$ the hypothesis is literally the assertion
\eqref{eq:forced-correlation} that the conclusion forces; there is no room
left for a counterexample of the same kind.

\paragraph{Derivation from the cited self-test.}
Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ satisfy the hypotheses.  Conditioning on
the orientation in which the first player receives the constraint gives a
strategy for the one-way linear constraint system game of value at least
$1-2\eps$, and at least $1-\eps$ if $\strategy$ is symmetric: writing
$p_{\mathrm A}$ and $p_{\mathrm B}$ for the success probabilities of the two
orientations, the value hypothesis reads
$\tfrac12 (p_{\mathrm A} + p_{\mathrm B}) \ge 1-\eps$, whence
$p_{\mathrm A} \ge 1-2\eps$ because $p_{\mathrm B} \le 1$, and
$p_{\mathrm A} = p_{\mathrm B} \ge 1-\eps$ when the two orientations are
exchanged by a symmetry of $\strategy$.  In neither case is the one-way value
determined; it is only bounded from below.  After a Naimark
dilation of both players' measurements, which does not change any Born
probability, \cite[Theorem~6.9]{Coladangelo2017Robust} applies to this
one-way strategy and yields $\phi_{\mathrm A}, \phi_{\mathrm B}, \ket\aux$ with
(\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~1) at scale $\sqrt\eps$ and with the relations for
the second player's variable observables, $\Id \ot \tilde B^{\Variable_1}_b
\approx_{\sqrt\eps} \Id \ot (\sigma^X_b)_{\mathrm B'}$ and likewise for
$\Variable_5$, after the local change of basis noted in the source.  (The
robust theorem is stated for projective measurements; the passage from the
dilated projections back to the original effects costs the leakage of the
dilated operators out of the range of the dilation, which is bounded by the
cell-consistency masses of a strategy of value $1-\eps$, as in the transfer
layer of the formalization.)  For the first player, the hypothesis gives
\[
  (\tilde A^{\Variable_j}_b \ot \Id)\,\phi\ket\psi
  = \phi\,(A^{\Variable_j}_b \ot \Id)\ket\psi
  \approx_{\sqrt\delta}
  \phi\,(\Id \ot B^{\Variable_j}_b)\ket\psi
  = (\Id \ot \tilde B^{\Variable_j}_b)\,\phi\ket\psi,
\]
where $\phi = \phi_{\mathrm A} \ot \phi_{\mathrm B}$ and $\approx_{\sqrt\delta}$
is closeness in norm; the second player's relation and
(\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~1) move the right-hand side to
$(\Id \ot \sigma^W_b)\ket\Theta$, and
$(\Id \ot \sigma^W_b)\ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2} = (\sigma^W_b \ot \Id)\ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2}$
because $\sigma^X_b$ and $\sigma^Z_b$ are real symmetric.  Every operator
involved is a contraction, so the first player's relations hold in norm at
scale $\sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta$, hence as $\approx_\eta$ estimates of the
squared distance.  The anticommutation consequences follow from the four
relations as in the source: $(\tilde A^{\Variable_1}\tilde A^{\Variable_5}
\ot \Id)\ket\Theta$ is within $O(\eta)$ of
$(\sigma^X\sigma^Z \ot \Id)\ket\Theta$ by replacing the two factors one at a
time, the second replacement using the same transposition identity to move
$\sigma^Z$ to the other side where it commutes with $\tilde A^{\Variable_1}$;
the reversed product is within $O(\eta)$ of
$(\sigma^Z\sigma^X \ot \Id)\ket\Theta = -(\sigma^X\sigma^Z \ot \Id)\ket\Theta$.
Bounds of order $\eta$ in norm are bounds of order $\eta^2 \le 2(\eps+\delta)
\le 2\eta$ in the squared distance for $\eta \le 1$, and for $\eta > 1$ every
estimate is trivial, so one universal constant serves all parameters.

\paragraph{The formal route.}
The formalization does not import the cited theorem.  Its rigidity chain
(\ghissue{101}--\ghissue{104}) works on the projective dilation of an
arbitrary strategy and derives, from the value alone, the approximate
anticommutation of each player's own $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$
reflections on the dilated state
(\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msVarObsA\_anticommute} and its
counterpart for the second player), together with exact swap isometries built
from those reflections and transfer theorems that pull every post-isometry
estimate back from the dilation to the original strategy at the cost of the
cell-consistency masses.  What the value cannot give is that the two players'
reflections agree on the dilated state, which the joint extraction of
$\ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2} \ot \ket\aux$ needs.  This is exactly what the hypothesis
supplies: the defect \eqref{eq:defect} of the original measurements transfers
to the dilated reflections through the same leakage bounds,
\[
  \bigl\| \bigl( X_{\mathrm A} \ot \Id - \Id \ot X_{\mathrm B} \bigr)
    \ket{\psi'} \bigr\|^2 \le 864\,\eps + 6\,\delta
\]
for the dilated $\Variable_j$ reflections $X_{\mathrm A}, X_{\mathrm B}$ on the
dilated state $\ket{\psi'}$
(\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msVarObsA\_close\_msVarObsB}).  In
this route the hypothesis enters through the state estimate
(\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~1), and all operator relations then follow for both
players alike; this is why the corrected statement carries $\eta$ uniformly.
The assembly along this route, owned by \ghissue{105}, is carried out;
Section~\ref{sec:formal} records the form it has.

\section{Sufficiency for the source's application}
\label{sec:sufficiency}

The only use of the theorem is in the analysis of the Pauli basis test.%
\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
lines~160--172 for the general strategy $\strategy = (\ket\psi, M)$ and its
projective dilation, lines~197--265 for Lemma~\path{lem:qld-win-implications}, and
lines~326--350 for the invocation.}
There, for each anticommuting tuple $\omega$, the measurements of the test
strategy for the Magic Square questions labelled by $\omega$ form a strategy
$\strategy_\omega = (\ket\psi, M^{\cdot,\omega})$ for $\game^{\MS}$ of value
$\Lambda_\omega = 1 - \eps_\omega$ with $\E_\omega \eps_\omega = O(\eps)$
(item~6 of the lemma), and the theorem is invoked for each $\omega$ to obtain
$\Id \ot M^{\Variable_1,\omega} M^{\Variable_5,\omega}
\approx_{\sqrt{\eps_\omega}} -\Id \ot M^{\Variable_5,\omega} M^{\Variable_1,\omega}$,
the anticommutation consequence for the second player, which is then
averaged over $\omega$ with Jensen's inequality.  The corrected theorem needs
in addition the agreement distances $\Delta_1(\strategy_\omega)$ and
$\Delta_5(\strategy_\omega)$.
They are available from the lemma, but three transports are needed besides the
triangle inequality, and they are worth spelling out.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Question distribution.}  Item~7 averages over \emph{anticommuting}
  $\omega$: it states that the first player's trace-postprocessed point
  measurement $\{P^{X,\omega}_a\}$, the $X$-basis point measurement at
  $u_X$ postprocessed by $a \mapsto \tr(a\,r_X)$ --- where
  $\omega = (u_X, u_Z, r_X, r_Z)$ --- agrees with the second
  player's $\Variable_1$ measurement,
  $P^{X,\omega}_a \ot \Id \simeq_\eps \Id \ot M^{\Variable_1,\omega}_a$.
  Item~1, by contrast, averages over the \emph{full} question distribution of
  the Pauli basis test and gives the self-consistency of the point
  measurements only under that distribution.  Combining the two therefore
  requires first conditioning item~1 on the anticommutation event and on the
  point question type.  Both are events of probability bounded below by a
  universal constant --- for the anticommutation event this is
  \path{fact:omega-anticomm-prob} --- and the quantity being averaged is
  nonnegative, so conditioning multiplies the bound by the reciprocal of that
  probability and item~1 holds on average over anticommuting $\omega$ at the
  cost of a constant factor.
  \item \emph{Postprocessing and observables.}  Item~1 concerns the point
  measurements $\{M^{(\mathsf{Point},W),u}_a\}$, whose outcomes are field
  elements, whereas the defect \eqref{eq:defect} involves binary measurements:
  the trace postprocessing on the point side and, on the Magic Square side, the
  relabeling of the game's answers to a bit. For projective measurements on
  opposite registers, the summed squared distance is twice the consistency
  defect. Coarse-graining preserves projectivity and decreases that defect:
  it removes nonnegative terms from the sum over disagreeing outcomes.
  Thus it does not increase the distance in this application. This argument
  does not assert distance monotonicity for arbitrary POVM effects.
  The passage between effects and observables uses the binary normalization
  identity, which is what the Lean form of
  item~1 requires: \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.pointObs\_self\_consistent} compares
  the two players' $\pm1$-valued point observables under the uniform
  distribution on the point $u$, while \eqref{eq:defect} is a sum over the two
  effects.  For a two-outcome projective measurement the effects are
  $(\Id \pm \mathcal O)/2$, so the summed squared effect distance is one half
  of the squared observable distance, and the two forms differ by a factor
  $2$.
  \item \emph{Swapped state.}  The defect \eqref{eq:defect} compares
  $A^{\Variable_j}_b \ot \Id$ with $\Id \ot B^{\Variable_j}_b$ on $\ket\psi$ in
  one orientation only.  The lemma's final clause supplies the reversed
  orientation, and its Lean form states that reversed estimate on the swapped
  state, the image of $\ket\psi$ under the exchange of the two tensor factors.
  Transporting an estimate from the swapped state back to $\ket\psi$ is that
  same exchange applied to the operators as well; it is an isometry, so the
  estimate is preserved.
\end{enumerate}
With the three transports in place, two applications of the triangle
inequality --- routed through the two point measurements, in the
$\approx_\eps$ form supplied by the lemma's own final clause --- give
$M^{\Variable_1,\omega}_a \ot \Id \approx_\eps \Id \ot M^{\Variable_1,\omega}_a$
on average over anticommuting $\omega$, that is,
$\E_\omega \Delta_1(\strategy_\omega) = O(\eps)$, and likewise for
$\Variable_5$ with the $Z$-basis point measurement.  Applying the corrected
theorem with $\delta_\omega = \Delta_1(\strategy_\omega) +
\Delta_5(\strategy_\omega)$ gives the anticommutation with error
$\sqrt{\eps_\omega} + \sqrt{\delta_\omega}$, and Jensen's inequality bounds its
average by $\sqrt{\E\eps_\omega} + \sqrt{\E\delta_\omega} = O(\sqrt\eps)$,
which is the bound the source obtains.  The application thus goes through with
the two triangle inequalities and the three transports above, and no new
input.

The Lean side of the application confirms both halves of this.  The induced
strategy \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ProjectiveSetting.msStrategyAt} is an
arbitrary strategy of \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame} with separate local
spaces for the two players, not a symmetric strategy, which is why the
corrected theorem is stated for arbitrary strategies; and the two consistency
inputs above are the statements
\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.win\_ms\_cons\_approx} (item~7, both orientations, in
the $\approx$ form) and \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.pointObs\_self\_consistent}
(item~1, in observable form) of
\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/WinImplications.lean}, from which the

that a named theorem assembling that average is already present. The current
Lean consumer takes a shorter route:
\leanid{WinImplications.\allowbreak msVarObs\_\allowbreak anticommutator\_le}
and \leanid{WinImplications.\allowbreak msVarObsA\_\allowbreak anticommutator\_le}

\section{Comparison with the blueprint and formalization}
\label{sec:formal}

The blueprint \cite{MIPStarREBlueprint} states \path{thm:ms-rigidity} in the
corrected form of item~4 of Section~2, with the hypothesis \eqref{eq:defect}
displayed and the source's unrestricted statement, its refutation, and the
derivation above recorded in the proof and in the remark that follows the
theorem.  The Lean declaration \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists\_ms\_rigidity}
carries the same statement: it quantifies over $\eps, \delta \ge 0$ and an
arbitrary strategy of \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msGame} of value at least
$1-\eps$ whose defects \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msVariableConsistencyDefect} at
the cells $0$ and $4$ (the paper's $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$) are at most
$\delta$, and concludes seven estimates for the relabeled bit effects at scale
$C(\sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta)$ for one universal constant $C$, with the witness
and distance definitions unchanged.  The statement-level \verb|\leanok| records
that the Lean statement matches the blueprint statement, and the proof-level
\verb|\leanok| records that the Lean proof of that statement is complete, with
the universal constant $C = 2 \cdot 10^{12}$.  Three companions accompany it.
\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msVariableConsistencyDefect\_eq\_zero\_of\_isConsistent}
shows that a symmetric strategy whose measurements are consistent on its state
has zero agreement distances, and
\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msVarObsA\_close\_msVarObsB}
transfers the hypothesis to the dilated reflections; both are sorry-free.
\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists\_ms\_rigidity\_of\_symmetric\_consistent} derives
from the theorem its specialization to the symmetric consistent strategies of
\path{def:consistent-strategy}, with the source's error scale; it
assumes projectivity as well, so that its hypothesis names exactly the source's
class and covers in particular the SPCC strategies of \path{def:spcc}, and its
own derivation is complete, so that with the theorem above proved it carries a
proof-level completion mark as well.  The blueprint records these as
\path{def:ms-variable-agreement}, \path{lem:ms-variable-agreement-zero},
\path{lem:ms-varobs-cross-player}, \path{lem:ms-variable-agreement-support} and
\path{cor:ms-rigidity-symmetric-consistent}.

The blueprint departs from the source in one further respect, smaller and
not mathematical, which is recorded here for the same reason.  The source
reads the relation $M \approx_\zeta N$ between operators that are not POVM
elements on the original state, as
$\bra{\psi}(M-N)^\dagger(M-N)\ket{\psi} \le O(\zeta)$.%
\footnote{\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
lines~644--646.}
The operators to which the source applies that relation are the products
$\tilde A^{\Variable_1} \tilde A^{\Variable_5} \ot \Id_{\mathrm{B'B''}}$ of the
transported observables, which act on
$\mH_{\mathrm A'} \ot \mH_{\mathrm A''} \ot \mH_{\mathrm B'} \ot
\mH_{\mathrm B''}$ and cannot be evaluated on $\ket{\psi}$ at all; the state
is therefore forced to be the extracted ideal state
$\ket{\Theta} = \ket{\EPR_2}^{\ot 2} \ot \ket{\aux}$ of
(\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~1).  The blueprint says so where it states the
convention, and \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msAnticommutatorDistanceA} and
\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.msAnticommutatorDistanceB} are accordingly defined on
\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.idealMsState}.  The difference is a local slip of the
source rather than a mathematical divergence, the intended reading being
forced by the domains of the operators; it is nonetheless a difference
between the formal statement and the printed one, so it is written down.

The assembly of the corrected theorem from the chain, which \ghissue{105}
owned, is carried out: the approximate anticommutation and cross-commutation
of a second logical pair for each player, by the same solution-group
computation along a second closed path of constraints; the joint
swap-isometry extraction of the two EPR pairs from each player's two
anticommuting pairs and from the cross-player agreement above, giving
(\path{thm:ms-rigidity},~1) at scale $\sqrt\eps + \sqrt\delta$; the
intertwining of each player's extracted qubit observables with $\sigma^X$ and
$\sigma^Z$; and the post-isometry transfers.  Nothing in it needs symmetry,
and nothing needs consistency beyond the two defects in the hypothesis.

The two players are not symmetric in that construction, and the asymmetry is
forced by the corrected hypothesis rather than chosen for convenience.  Bob's
second logical pair is his variable reflections at the cells of the paper's

(\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msVarObsB\_second\_pair\_anticommute}).
Alice's second pair is not the corresponding pair of her variable reflections:

(\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msCellObsA\_second\_pair\_anticommute}),

\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.MagicSquareRigidity.msCellObsA\_close\_msVarObsB}, an
orientation which the question distribution does sample; so no hypothesis
beyond \eqref{eq:defect} is needed for it.

\section{Necessity, error scales, and the adoption boundary}
\label{sec:adoption}

The zero-error obstruction establishes the necessity of agreement at both
distinguished variables for the full extraction conclusion. It does not
establish either a necessary hypothesis for same-player anticommutation or an
optimal robustness exponent. These are different assertions.

To see that agreement at just one variable is insufficient, keep the canonical
state $\ket\Omega$ and the canonical constraint measurements of Alice and
variable measurements of Bob. On the reverse orientation conjugate Alice's
entire variable solution by $U=\exp(-i\theta\sigma^Z/2)\ot\Id$, and Bob's
entire constraint solution by $\overline U$. The identity
$(T\ot\Id)\ket\Omega=(\Id\ot T^{\mathsf T})\ket\Omega$ shows that each
orientation still wins perfectly. The distinguished variable observables of
Alice are now $(\cos\theta\,\sigma^X+\sin\theta\,\sigma^Y)\ot\Id$ and
$\sigma^Z\ot\Id$. Consequently
\[
  \Delta_1=1-\cos\theta,\qquad \Delta_5=0.
\]
Conjugation about $\sigma^X$ exchanges the two conclusions. Thus neither
agreement condition can be omitted at zero error. Both examples retain exact
same-player anticommutation. They may also be symmetrized by the role flags
of Section~\ref{sec:symmetric}, without changing either defect.

There is a quantitative distinction as well. Write
$\ket{\Psi'}=(\phi_A\ot\phi_B)\ket\psi$, let
$s=\|\ket{\Psi'}-\ket\Theta\|$, and let $d_{A,j},d_{B,j}$ be the two
summed squared measurement distances on $\ket\Theta$. For the complete
binary effects, isometric transport, contraction, and the triangle inequality
in the direct sum of the two outcome spaces give
\begin{equation}
  \Delta_j \le 24s^2+3d_{A,j}+3d_{B,j},\qquad
  d_{A,j}\le 24s^2+3\Delta_j+3d_{B,j}.
  \label{eq:agreement-transfer}
\end{equation}
Indeed, the two ideal effects act identically on $\ket\Theta$. Subtract their
actions, insert $\ket{\Psi'}$, and use
$\|\tilde A_b\ot\Id-\Id\ot\tilde B_b\|\le2$ for each of two outcomes.
The squared three-term triangle inequality gives the constant $24$.

In particular, the printed estimates force only
$\Delta_j=O(\sqrt\eps)$ by this argument, not $O(\eps)$.
Conversely, a one-way extraction with $s=O(\sqrt\eps)$ and
$d_{B,j}=O(\sqrt\eps)$ would give
$d_{A,j}=O(\sqrt\eps+\Delta_j)$ in the small-error regime. Its state and
Bob's measurement estimates do not need an agreement term. In the rotation
example the identity isometries already have $s=d_{B,1}=d_{B,5}=0$ and
$d_{A,j}=\Delta_j$. Hence the uniform use of $\sqrt\delta$ in all seven
bounds is a sufficient consequence of the existing construction, not an
established minimal loss. No optimality claim for all strategies follows from
this example.

The source's sole invocation of rigidity is the same-player anticommutation
step in \path{len:qld-win-implications-obs}. After replacement by the proved
original-state bound, its output and both tensor orientations are unchanged.
All later uses depend on that output: \path{lem:qld-comm-cons}, the combined
point and line measurements, the global polynomial pair, the construction of
Pauli measurements and the swap unitary, and finally \path{thm:pauli} and
\path{cor:pauli-binary}. The source's later introspection use of the latter
therefore has the same input. This is sufficiency with respect to this gap;
it does not discharge the separate line, error-function, or decoding gaps.
The full source and blueprint inventory, including conditional nodes and
the formalization-only specialization, is in the accompanying audit.

The secondary source does not silently supply the missing hypothesis. Its
oracularized game explicitly adds same-cell consistency questions with
constant probability
(\path{references/neexp-paper/07_a_self_test_for_the_pauli_basis.tex:100-116}).
Those edges are absent from $\game^{\MS}$. Importing them would change the
game, and no such change is made here.

\section{Prescribed answers and the retained printed claim}
\label{sec:prescribed}

There is a further representation comparison. Write
$A_{j,b}=A^{\Variable_j}_{\mathsf{bit}(b)}$ for the prescribed bit effect and
$R_{A,j}=\sum_\beta A^{\Variable_j}_{\mathsf{triple}(\beta)}$ for the
wrong-form mass operator; define $B_{j,b},R_{B,j}$ similarly. The effects in
the proved theorem are
\[
  \hat A_{j,0}=A_{j,0}+R_{A,j},\qquad
  \hat A_{j,1}=A_{j,1},
\]
and likewise for Bob, because \leanid{msBitOrZero} sends every triple to zero.
The source's four displayed estimates name the prescribed effects themselves.
The retention declaration
\leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.PrintedMagicSquareRigidityClaim} in
\path{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/MagicSquareTheorems/PrintedClaim.lean}
therefore uses $A_{j,b},B_{j,b}$ directly, and uses their differences for both
anticommutators. It quantifies over every strategy of value exactly $1-\eps$,
with one universal constant for all seven bounds at scale $\sqrt\eps$.
It is a definition of a proposition, with no proof and no new hypothesis.
Both counterexamples have only prescribed answers, so this distinction cannot
remove their contradiction.

The existing lemmas in the namespace \leanid{MagicSquareRigidity},
\leanid{alice\_variable\_\allowbreak wrong\_form\_mass\_le} and
\leanid{bob\_variable\_\allowbreak wrong\_form\_mass\_le}, bound
$\langle R_{A,j}\ot\Id\rangle_\psi$ and
$\langle\Id\ot R_{B,j}\rangle_\psi$ by $36\eps$. Since $0\le R\le\Id$,
the norm of its action on $\ket\psi$ is at most $6\sqrt\eps$. On an extracted
ideal state at distance $s$, it is at most $6\sqrt\eps+s$. Thus the summed
squared prescribed-effect distance is at most
\[
  2d_{A,j}+2(6\sqrt\eps+s)^2,
\]
and similarly for Bob. This supplies the mathematical effect-transfer
estimate. Transferring the products in the two anticommutators additionally
requires moving the other variable observable to its opposite-player
constraint counterpart before applying the wrong-form bound; a bound on
$R\ket\psi$ alone is not a bound on $RO\ket\psi$.
For example, put $O_j=A_{j,0}-A_{j,1}$ and
$\hat O_j=O_j+R_{A,j}$. The difference of the two anticommutators is
\[
  R_{A,1}\hat O_5+O_1R_{A,5}
    +R_{A,5}\hat O_1+O_5R_{A,1}.
\]
The two terms with $R$ on the right are bounded by $6\sqrt\eps$ each.
In a term $R_{A,1}\hat O_5\ket\psi$, replace $\hat O_5$ by Bob's
constraint observable for that cell, at cost $O(\sqrt\eps)$ from the sampled
constraint--variable consistency test. It commutes with $R_{A,1}$, so the
remaining norm is again at most $6\sqrt\eps$. The other term is identical.
This proves that the value-only anticommutator estimate also supplies the
source's prescribed-answer anticommutation, with a universal changed constant;
the assembled Lean prescribed-answer extraction theorem remains a separate
target below.

An explicit remaining construction target is the prescribed-answer version
of \leanid{exists\_ms\_rigidity}: the same value and two agreement hypotheses,
the same witness shape, and all seven bounds for the uncompleted effects at
$C'(\sqrt\eps+\sqrt\delta)$. A second target for assessing minimality is a
one-way extraction from value alone, retaining the $O(\sqrt\eps)$ state
bound and Bob's variable estimates, with Alice's constraint-read estimates;
\eqref{eq:agreement-transfer} then transfers only the required variable
comparisons. Neither target is an added theorem assumption or an asserted
Lean result in this change. They do not make the unrestricted printed claim
true, nor do they alone authorize a terminal register row.

\section{Conclusion}

The unrestricted extraction assertion is false, even for symmetric perfect
strategies, and is now retained unasserted with its prescribed answers.
The robust theorem with agreement defects is proved, and the source's
soundness use is supplied by the stronger value-only anticommutation lemmas.
The additional agreement hypothesis, the uniform enlarged error, and the
completed bit effects must nevertheless be compared separately with the
printed extraction assertion. Historical decision B5 is not a certification
of the current four adoption conditions. The row remains pending: no game,
source semantics, completion criterion, or terminal status is changed.

Each of those embeddings composes two one-qubit controlled swaps, one for each of two logical pairs of that player's $\pm 1$ reflections on the dilated state, and the two players' pairs are not chosen symmetrically. Bob's are his variable reflections at the cells of $\mathsf{Variable}_1$ and $\mathsf{Variable}_5$ and at those of $\mathsf{Variable}_2$ and $\mathsf{Variable}_4$. Alice's first pair is her variable reflections at the cells of $\mathsf{Variable}_1$ and $\mathsf{Variable}_5$, but her second is her \emph{constraint} reflections at the cells of $\mathsf{Variable}_2$ and $\mathsf{Variable}_4$, read from the first and from the second row. That asymmetry is forced by the hypothesis: \eqref{eq:ms-rigidity-consistency} compares the two players only at $\mathsf{Variable}_1$ and $\mathsf{Variable}_5$, so their $\mathsf{Variable}_2$ and $\mathsf{Variable}_4$ measurements cannot be compared, whereas Alice's constraint reflections at those two cells are compared with Bob's variable reflections there by a question pair that the distribution does sample. Item~1 is the joint state estimate on the dilation, which needs the approximate anticommutation of both of Alice's pairs, the cross-player agreement of all four pairs of corresponding reflections, and the approximate commutation of the two pairs of each player; the anticommutation of the second pair comes from a second closed path through the grid, which crosses the exceptional third column once and therefore returns the reversed product with the opposite sign. The bit-measurement relations come from the transport of the first logical pair through those embeddings, exactly for the phase observable and up to the anticommutator defect of that pair for the shift observable; the anticommutation consequences come from the solution-group computation on the dilation, products composing under conjugation by an isometry. Every conclusion is then moved from the dilated strategy to the original one by the leakage bounds of the dilation, with an explicit universal constant, which the formalization takes to be $2 \cdot 10^{12}$. The specialization to symmetric consistent strategies ($\delta = 0$) is stated as a separate declaration derived from it.

\begin{remark}[The strategy class in Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-rigidity}]\label{rem:ms-rigidity-strategy-class}
	Fix the canonical Mermin--Peres operator solution on $\C^2 \ot \C^2$ --- the nine $\pm 1$ observables $\sigma^X \ot I$, $I \ot \sigma^X$, $\sigma^X \ot \sigma^X$ in the first row, $I \ot \sigma^Z$, $\sigma^Z \ot I$, $\sigma^Z \ot \sigma^Z$ in the second, and $\sigma^X \ot \sigma^Z$, $\sigma^Z \ot \sigma^X$, $\sigma^Y \ot \sigma^Y$ in the third --- and let $\ket{\Omega}$ be the maximally entangled state of two copies of $\C^2 \ot \C^2$. Measuring the three commuting observables of a row or column on a $\mathsf{Constraint}$ question, and the single observable of a cell on a $\mathsf{Variable}$ question, is a symmetric, projective, consistent strategy of value $1$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}). Now give each player two copies of $\C^2 \ot \C^2$ paired into two copies of $\ket{\Omega}$, and split the two roles across them: on a constraint question the first player measures copy~$1$ and the second copy~$2$, and on a variable question the first player measures copy~$2$ and the second copy~$1$. Every sampled question pair consists of one constraint and one variable, so the two measurements actually performed are the canonical perfect pair acting on a single copy of $\ket{\Omega}$, and the value is $1$. The two players' $\mathsf{Variable}_1$ observables, however, act on halves of different copies, whose joint reduced state is a product of maximally mixed states, so their correlation is $0$, while the second item of Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-rigidity} forces it to be $1$ at $\eps = \delta = 0$; the same computation applies to $\mathsf{Variable}_5$. Giving each player a flag qubit, putting the two flags in the state $(\ket{01}+\ket{10})/\sqrt2$, and letting each player's flag select which of the two roles it plays turns this into a \emph{symmetric} strategy with the same value and the same vanishing correlations, so a restriction to symmetric strategies (Definition~\ref{def:symmetric-game}) would not repair the source's statement. Agreement of the two players' $\mathsf{Variable}_1$ and $\mathsf{Variable}_5$ measurements on the state, that is, the hypothesis~\eqref{eq:ms-rigidity-consistency} --- exact consistency in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:consistent-measurement} when the strategy is symmetric and $\delta = 0$ --- does force the correlation to be $1$ up to $O(\delta)$, and both strategies above have agreement distance $\Delta_1 = \Delta_5 = 1$ (Definition~\ref{def:ms-variable-agreement}). It is also what the analysis of the Pauli basis test has available when it applies Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-rigidity}: the Magic Square strategy induced at an anticommuting tuple has, on average over the tuple, agreement distances of order $\eps$ by items~1 and~7 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-win-implications} (the point measurements are consistent between the players, and each player's point measurement agrees with the other player's variable measurement), once item~1 is conditioned on the anticommutation event and both are passed through the binary relabeling of Definition~\ref{def:ms-variable-agreement}; that analysis uses only the anticommutation consequence for one player. The theorem is therefore stated with that agreement as its hypothesis, for arbitrary and not necessarily symmetric strategies; the class of symmetric consistent strategies named in the owner decision is the case $\delta = 0$. The details are in \cite{gap:qpbt_ms-rigidity-symmetric-strategies}.
\end{remark}

# Completion protocol — definition of done

Normative. This protocol says when a formalization **track** may be declared
finished, and forbids the declaration until a model-free gate agrees. Amend it
only through `local/protocols/meta.md` (`EVOLUTION.md` entry, cited trigger).

Trigger for its existence, owner, 2026-09-19: *"some protocol(s) in the
workflow should ensure that when the project finishes, the formalization is
done without caveat, and satisfies the lean comparator"*; earlier the same day,
*"i want zero sorry"*.

## 1. Scope

A **track** is a Lean subtree, the blueprint chapters describing it, its
paper-gap register, its axiom-audit file, its blueprint exemption table, its
comparator record and its artifact file set. The per-track data is §6; QPBT is
the only track registered
today, but nothing here is QPBT-specific.

**Declaring finished** means any public statement that the track is complete: a
completion comment on its umbrella issues (27/168 for QPBT), closing those
issues, tagging a release, or a README/status page that says the track is done.

## 2. Finished without caveat

A track is finished without caveat at a commit when all seven criteria hold *at
that commit*.

**C1 — Proof integrity.** Zero term-level `sorry`, `admit`, project `axiom` or
`constant` declaration, `native_decide` / `decide +native`, or
`Lean.trustCompiler` under the track's Lean root. The sorry-site rule is the
one in `results/telemetry/owner-tools/estimate.sh` (`SORRY_SITE_RE`), and there
is exactly **one** implementation of it: `scripts/completion_gate.py` loads that
line from that file and never restates it. Explicit axiom declarations are
found with `DECL_RE` of `scripts/audit_lean_axiom_declarations.py`, imported
rather than copied.

**C2 — Headline axioms.** Every headline theorem of §6 depends only on
`propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The check is a committed
`AxiomAudit` Lean file for the track that carries one audit command per
headline theorem — `assert_standard_axioms` (LDT) or `audit_standard_axioms`
(the command QPBT's audit module defines); both print the axiom set and fail
elaboration unless it is exactly those three — and is built in CI. The gate
checks that the file
exists and covers the table; the axiom values themselves come from the build
and are reported as delegated.

**C3 — Paper gaps terminal.** Every data row of the track's paper-gap register
carries a `Terminal status` cell reading exactly `corrected` or
`no-difference`:

- `corrected` — a documented statement correction that **meets the four
  adoption conditions of `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`** — correctness,
  sufficiency, minimality ("the closest sufficient statement to the source,
  with no unnecessary hypothesis or weakened conclusion and no change to the
  source semantics") and Lean convergence — and carries its three artifacts: a
  gap note, a corrected blueprint node citing it, and, where the printed claim
  is not proved, the printed claim preserved as a non-asserted `Prop` (the
  `lem:symmetric-strat` and `lem:qld-4-13` pattern of 2026-09-19). The
  artifacts are evidence that a correction was adopted; they are not a route
  around those conditions, and a row whose correction weakens a conclusion is
  not terminal however complete its artifacts are.
- `no-difference` — the formalization and the source statement agree; nothing
  to correct.

No row may read `open`, `pending` or `sorry`. No headline theorem statement may
be weaker than the source paper except through a `corrected` row.

**C4 — Blueprint marked.** Every blueprint node of the track that carries
`\lean{...}` also carries `\leanok`, or appears in the track's exemption table
with a written reason; `scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py --ci` exits 0. A
node is any environment the repository's blueprint parser recognises: the gate
reads that list out of `_TEX_ENV_BEGIN_RE` in `scripts/blueprint_lean_sync.py`
instead of keeping its own, so an `example` or `remark` node with a Lean link
counts exactly as a theorem does. Which nodes are the track's is read off the
tree and not off section 6: besides the chapters registered there, the gate
reads every other `.tex` beside them whose `\lean{...}` names a declaration
under the track's Lean root, and judges those nodes too, so a node of the track
that lives in a chapter shared with another track is in scope whether or not
its chapter is listed. The
exemption table is the only place a permanently unmarked node may live, and a
row there is a caveat that must be defensible in the paper.

**C5 — Lean comparator.** A comparator challenge exists covering every headline
theorem; the in-repository expected challenge is free of regeneration drift
(`scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py` for that track's expected copy
passes in CI); and the track's comparator record (§6, `docs/comparator.md`)
states the challenge repository, the library commit that repository last
verified with the official `leanprover/comparator` (`permitted_axioms` limited
to the three standard axioms, external kernel check enabled where the platform
allows), and the expected-copy path. That verified commit must be an
ancestor-or-equal of the commit being declared finished, with no Lean change to
the statement closure in between — which is exactly what a passing drift check
proves.

The coverage half of C5 is decided against the challenge, never against the
record alone. The record's `expected-challenge` must be exactly the expected
copy §6 registers for the track, and every headline theorem of §6 must occur in
that file or split challenge tree by its fully-qualified name — the name the assembler of
`scripts/comparator/` writes for each declaration of the closure. A record that
lists a headline theorem the registered expected copy never names fails C5:
`covered-theorems` is written by hand in the same document, by the same session
that wants to declare the track finished, so it may not be its own evidence.
That the challenge *elaborates* to the same statements is the drift check and
the comparator run, both delegated to CI.

**C6 — Docs truthful.** No README, status page or estimate may advertise a
nonzero open-site count once C1 holds. Every doc the track registers (§6) must
exist: a registered doc that has been renamed or deleted fails C6 rather than
being skipped, so the criterion can never report a green run over zero docs.

**C7 — Artifact readiness.** "Done" means ready to be attached as an artifact
to an ITP submission (owner, 2026-09-19), so every file such a submission needs
is committed at the declared commit: the files §6 registers for the track —
today `README.md`, `docs/QPBT-theorem-index.md`, `docs/DEVIATIONS.md`,
`docs/ARTIFACT.md` and `LICENSE` — and the snapshot script
`scripts/make_artifact.sh`. The gate checks that each of them exists and fails
closed naming the missing ones; that the script *produces* a snapshot whose
leak scan passes is a run, and is reported as delegated like C2, C4 and C5.
A missing artifact file is main's to-do list, not a caveat that may be carried
into a completion statement.

## 3. Where the comparator challenge lives

The challenge repository lives **outside** this repository and outside the
umbrella repository: a separate repository of its own, as `LDT-comparator`
already is for `MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.mainFormal` (`docs/comparator.md`). Three
reasons, in order of weight:

1. *Validating Proofs* level 4 requires the statement to be written in a
   trusted environment separate from the proof code. A challenge inside this
   repository would be elaborated in the same environment it is meant to check.
2. The challenge must depend on this library **pinned by commit**. A repository
   cannot meaningfully pin a commit of itself, and the pin is the evidence C5
   rests on.
3. `Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-qpbt` is the umbrella repository and is not the main
   session's to modify (`local/personas/main.md`).

What stays here: the generator (`scripts/comparator/`), the expected copy, the
drift check, and the comparator record. Creating the challenge repository is an
action outside this repository and is therefore an **owner action**, not a main
decision.

## 4. Who enforces this

The main session, or the acting main, **may not** post a completion statement
on the track's umbrella issues, close them, or tag a release unless

    python3 scripts/completion_gate.py check --track <track>

exits 0 on the exact commit being declared, and the gate's output is attached
to the completion comment. A gate run on any other commit is not evidence.

A failing gate is **not an owner blocker**. It is main's to-do list: no owner
inbox comment is filed for it, and the work it names is ordinary development.

The gate is deliberately **not** part of the blocking PR CI: it would fail every
PR until the comparator challenge exists. `local/bin/ci.sh` has no non-blocking
step class — every step it records is blocking — so CI is left unchanged, and
the gate is run by hand before a completion statement.

## 5. The gate

`scripts/completion_gate.py` is python3, standard library only, no network and
no model call. `check --track <t> [--repo-root R] [--commit C] [--json]` prints
one PASS/FAIL line per criterion with `file:line` evidence, and exits 0 only
when every mechanically checkable criterion passes. Criteria with a half that
needs a run the gate does not perform (C2 axiom values, C4 `--ci` run, C5 drift
regeneration, C7 snapshot leak scan) print as
`DELEGATED` once their static half holds — never as `PASS`, so no completion
comment can quote a green line for a check nobody ran — while a failing static
half is still `FAIL`. `DELEGATED` does not turn a failing run green and does
not by itself make one green either: the delegated halves are read off the CI
run of the same commit. Unit tests:
`scripts/tests/test_completion_gate.py`.

## 6. Registered tracks

### QPBT

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Lean root | `MIPStarRE/QPBT` |
| Blueprint chapters | `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex` |
| Paper-gap register | `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt-gap-register.md` |
| Axiom audit | `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Test/AxiomAudit.lean` |
| `\leanok` exemptions | `docs/completion/qpbt-leanok-exemptions.md` |
| Comparator record | `docs/comparator.md`, block `track=qpbt` |
| Expected challenge | `scripts/comparator/expected/qpbt` |
| Truthful docs (C6) | `README.md` |
| Artifact files (C7) | `README.md`, `docs/QPBT-theorem-index.md`, `docs/DEVIATIONS.md`, `docs/ARTIFACT.md`, `LICENSE` |
| Artifact script (C7) | `scripts/make_artifact.sh` |
| Umbrella issues | 27, 168 |

Headline theorems (blueprint chapter `ch13_qpbt_test.tex`):

| Lean name | Blueprint node |
|---|---|
| `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness` | `thm:pauli` |
| `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit` | `cor:pauli-binary` |
| `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one` | `lem:pauli-completeness` |
| `MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness` | `lem:ld-soundness` |

The expected challenge is the split tree generated from
`scripts/comparator/challenges/qpbt.json`: its root `Challenge.lean` and
mirrored modules together must name all four headline declarations above.
The gate reads every Lean file in that registered tree, checks coverage against
the headline table rather than the hand-written comparator record, and still
requires the record's expected-copy path to agree exactly. Comparator
verification remains delegated evidence: the record must name a verified
ancestor revision, the official run must permit only the three standard
axioms, and the drift check must establish agreement at the completion commit.

The `Blueprint chapters` row is the track's own chapters, read whole; it is
not the whole of C4's scope. The gate also reads every other `.tex` file in
those directories whose `\lean{...}` names a declaration under the track's
Lean root and judges those nodes — today
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch03_preliminaries.tex` carries one such QPBT node — so
a chapter missing from the row above narrows nothing.

Adding a track means adding its row set here and its entry in the gate's
`TRACKS` registry, in one commit; a unit test reads this section and fails if a
registry entry names a path these rows do not. That test reads every
path-valued field of `Track` — every row above but the umbrella issues — and
fails as well when `Track` gains or loses a field without a line in the test,
so the rule cannot quietly stop covering part of the registry.
